info.title: Chrona Audit API
info.description: The stable part of the audit-api. A stable route only changes additively: new optional request fields, new response fields, new routes. Clients must ignore response fields they do not know. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: exchange an API token for one at `POST /auth/token`. Routes not listed here exist but may change without notice.

Error.description: Any error. Below 500: `{ error: <code>, detail? }`; 500: `{ error: "internal_error", requestId }`.

post.summary: Exchange an API token for a short-lived JWT
post.description: Mint an API token under Account → API tokens (`POST /account/api-tokens`), keep its secret, and exchange it here for a JWT that is valid for 15 minutes. Send the JWT as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every other call, and exchange again when it expires. The JWT is bound to the organisation the token was minted in. This route needs no Authorization header.

access_token.description: A signed JWT. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

401.description: `invalid_token`: unknown or revoked token, or its minter left the organisation.

schema.description: `invalid_token`: unknown or revoked token, or its minter left the organisation.

post.summary: Trade a sign-in session for a token naming one organisation
post.description: For interactive sign-in sessions that do not yet name an organisation: pick one the user belongs to and receive a JWT for it. A token that already names an organisation (such as one from `POST /auth/token`) is refused.

access_token.description: A signed JWT. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

403.description: `not_a_session_token`, `not_a_member` or `sso_required` (the organisation requires single sign-on and this session did not come from it).

schema.description: `not_a_session_token`, `not_a_member` or `sso_required` (the organisation requires single sign-on and this session did not come from it).

get.summary: The caller’s own API tokens, grouped by organisation
get.description: Lists the signed-in person’s API tokens in every organisation they belong to, live tokens first. With `orgId`, only that organisation is listed and `offset` pages through its tokens (50 per page); without it each organisation shows its first page. `incomplete` is true when some organisation could not be read. Only a person may call this, not an API token.

revokedAt.description: null while the token is live.

tokenHint.description: Shortened form of the secret (`makia_AbCd…WxYz`); null for old tokens.

total.description: All tokens the caller has in this organisation.

post.summary: Mint an API token in an organisation
post.description: Creates an API token for the signed-in person in the named organisation. The `secret` is shown only in this answer; store it, then exchange it at `POST /auth/token` for a JWT. Only a person may call this, not an API token.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the caller’s own API tokens
delete.description: The organisation and token id go in the query string. A revoked token can no longer be exchanged.

404.description: `not_found`: no such live token of the caller’s.

schema.description: `not_found`: no such live token of the caller’s.

delete.summary: Delete a case and everything under it
delete.description: Removes the case with its documents, runs and findings. Runs still queued or running are stopped first; a running one gets a short bounded wait to wind down, then the case is deleted regardless. Deleting a case that is already gone also answers 204. Needs the `cases` permission.

post.summary: Declare a set of files you are about to upload
post.description: Step 1 of a tracked upload. Send the file names, sizes and (optionally) sha256 hashes of everything you intend to upload for one workflow input (`inputId`, a source node of the case’s workflow version). No file bytes are sent here. The answer judges each file: send the bytes of those marked `ready`; `already_in_case`, `too_large` and `rejected` need nothing. Step 2: for each `ready` file, upload the bytes with `POST /documents?caseId=…&inputId=…&batchId=<batchId>&itemId=<itemId>` (multipart, field `file`), using the `itemId` from this answer; that upload marks the item as landed. Step 3: when all uploads have finished, call `POST /upload-batches/{id}/finalize`. The server compares the declared set with what arrived and closes the batch as `complete` or `incomplete` (a file declared but never uploaded is a gap). A batch whose client never finalizes is closed as abandoned after a while. Batches are optional: `POST /documents` also works alone. At most 1000 files per batch.

itemId.description: Pass as `itemId` when uploading this file to POST /documents.

superseded.description: For `already_in_case`: the case holds these bytes but they were replaced in the bucket, so runs do not use them.

files.description: One entry per declared file, in the order sent.

post.summary: Close an upload batch
post.description: Step 3 of a tracked upload (see POST /cases/{id}/upload-batches). The status is computed from the item states, not taken from the caller: `incomplete` when any file is still `pending` or `failed`, else `complete`. Calling it again with nothing changed returns the same answer with `replayed: true`; a batch already closed differently (for example abandoned) answers 409.

409.description: `batch_not_open`: the batch was closed another way; `detail.status` says how.

schema.description: `batch_not_open`: the batch was closed another way; `detail.status` says how.

post.summary: Upload one file into a case
post.description: Send the file as `multipart/form-data` in a field named `file`; `caseId`, `inputId` (a source node of the case’s workflow version) and optional `tags` (a JSON object of strings, checked against the source node’s tag rules) go in the query string. Uploading the same bytes to the same case again is safe: it answers 201 with `deduplicated: true` and the existing document. Files above the size cap answer 413. Optionally pass `batchId` and `itemId` together to mark the file in an upload batch. Needs the `cases` permission.

deduplicated.description: The case already held these bytes.

workflowDefault.description: The bytes are this input’s workflow default file.

superseded.description: With `deduplicated`: the case holds these bytes but they were replaced in the bucket, so runs do not use them.

409.description: `workflow_default_file`: the bytes are another input’s default file.

schema.description: `workflow_default_file`: the bytes are another input’s default file.

get.summary: The documents of a case, oldest first
get.description: Every document the case holds, uploaded or pulled from storage, and those a run derived from another (`parentDocumentId`). `superseded` marks bytes that were replaced in their storage bucket: runs skip them. Filter by `inputId` (the workflow input the file was given for). Page with `limit` (1–1000, default 500) and `offset`; `total` is the count over the whole filter. Fetch the bytes with GET /documents/{id}/content.

inputId.description: The workflow source node the file was uploaded for.

parentDocumentId.description: Set on a document a run derived from another one.

post.summary: Start a run over a case
post.description: Send `{caseId}` to run the case’s workflow version; the answer carries the new run’s id and the run is queued. Poll GET /runs/{id} until its status is terminal. Optional: `parameters` (workflow parameter values), `triggeredBy` (service accounts only: a display label for who on your side caused the run), `skipCache`, `useReviewMemory`, `oneShot`, `artifactOverrides`. The `inlineGraph`, `projectId`, `inlineCaseInputs` and `ephemeral` fields are for internal tooling that runs an unpublished graph; exactly one of `caseId` or `inlineGraph` is required.

400.description: `invalid_input`, `triggered_by_not_allowed` (a person set triggeredBy), `selection_refused`, or a parameter error (`unknown_parameter`, `missing_required_parameter`, …).

schema.description: `invalid_input`, `triggered_by_not_allowed` (a person set triggeredBy), `selection_refused`, or a parameter error (`unknown_parameter`, `missing_required_parameter`, …).

403.description: The caller lacks the project’s `run` permission.

schema.description: The caller lacks the project’s `run` permission.

get.summary: List runs, newest first
get.description: The runs the caller can see in the token’s org. Filter by `caseId`, `projectId`, `workflowId` (a project workflow) and `status` (repeatable: `?status=failed&status=paused`); filters combine with AND. Page with `limit` (1–200, default 50) and `offset`; `total` is the count over the whole filter. Each run is the one GET /runs/{id} answers, without `nodeExecutions` and `findingReviewBatches`. Scratch runs of internal tooling (`ephemeral`) are not listed.

status.description: queued → running → succeeded | failed | cancelled. `paused` = parked for human review until POST /runs/{id}/resume. Terminal (stop polling): succeeded, failed, cancelled. A stop requested on a running run keeps `running` until the worker unwinds (see `cancelRequestedAt`).

triggeredBy.description: The label a service-account caller gave for its own user, if any.

parameters.description: The resolved workflow parameters the run started with.

finishedAt.description: Set once the run is terminal.

pausedAt.description: Set while the run is parked for review.

activeMs.description: Active run time in ms; null until the run is terminal.

costMicroUsd.description: Decimal as a string; null until the run is terminal.

findingsCount.description: Total findings; null until the run is terminal.

workflowId.description: The project workflow the run’s version belongs to; null for an inline-graph run.

get.summary: A run’s status and node executions
get.description: Poll this for progress. `status` runs queued → running → succeeded | failed | cancelled; `paused` means parked for human review (resume with POST /runs/{id}/resume). Terminal statuses: succeeded, failed, cancelled. `findingsCount`, `activeMs` and the cost fields are null until the run is terminal. A run that failed at graph load has an empty `nodeExecutions` list.

post.summary: Request that a run stop
post.description: A queued or paused run becomes `cancelled` at once. A running run answers `cancelling`: the worker unwinds within a few seconds and the run then turns `cancelled`; keep polling GET /runs/{id}. A run that is already terminal answers its own status (no-op).

status.description: `cancelling` = the stop is requested but the run is still winding down.

get.summary: Resolve evidence references to citations
get.description: Records and findings carry evidence as 16-hex references. Pass up to 100 of them as `refs` (comma separated). The answer is a map keyed by reference to its citation: the document id, the quoted text, where it sits on the page, a locator and whether the quote was found in the document. A reference the run does not hold, or one that is not 16 hex characters, is left out of the map. 503 means no worker answered; retry later.

quote.description: `{exact, prefix, suffix}` of the cited text.

anchor.description: Where the quote sits, e.g. `{kind: "page_box", page, x0, y0, x1, y1}`.

post.summary: Resume a paused run after its review decisions
post.description: A paused run waits for human decisions on every parked item. Once they are made, this queues the resume; the run goes back to `running`. Needs the project’s `review` or `run` permission.

403.description: Neither `review` nor `run` permission on the project.

schema.description: Neither `review` nor `run` permission on the project.

409.description: `run_not_paused`, or the decisions are incomplete (`no_pending_resolutions` or a partial-node reason; `detail.nodes` lists the nodes).

schema.description: `run_not_paused`, or the decisions are incomplete (`no_pending_resolutions` or a partial-node reason; `detail.nodes` lists the nodes).

post.summary: Create a case from uploaded files and run the workflow, in one call
post.description: Authenticate with a service account’s API token (`Authorization: Bearer makia_…`); a person’s token is refused with 403 `service_account_required`. Send multipart/form-data: one or more file parts named after the workflow’s `source@1` input ids (at most 50 files), plus optional fields `name`, `tags`, `parameters`, `triggeredBy`. The latest published version of the workflow runs. An optional `Idempotency-Key` header (1–255 printable ASCII) makes a repeat call within 24 hours return the first answer, marked by an `idempotent-replayed: true` response header. Poll `status_url` (GET /runs/{id}) for the outcome; `review_url` is the run’s Studio page (null when the server has no public Studio address). An `external_id` field makes the call idempotent per workflow: a known one answers 200 with the existing case and run. `?rerun=1` (with a known `external_id`) adds the files to that case and starts a new run (202); without a known id it is 404 `case_not_found`. The files and parameters of a re-run are checked against, and the run uses, the case’s own workflow version, not the latest one; send `external_id` before the files then (else 400 `external_id_first`). An `Idempotency-Key` replay answers 202 with a header, an `external_id` replay answers 200. A repeated `external_id` field is 400 `duplicate_field`. **Files by reference**: send `Content-Type: application/json` instead, with `{external_id?, name?, parameters? (an object), triggeredBy?, sources}`; `sources` (1–50) are picks from a storage connection of the organization, the same shape as `POST /cases/{id}/imports` (`inputId`, `connectionId`, `prefix` or `paths`, `include`, `tags`, `rulesets`). Uploads and sources never mix in one call: the content type decides. The case and its picks are written and the import is queued; the 202 carries `run_id` and `import_id` at once, but the run starts only when the import ends: `GET /runs/{run_id}` answers 404 until then. Every announced run ends in the change feed: an import that fails or lands no file ends it `failed` with a `run.failed` event whose `ref.error_code` is `inbound_import_failed` or `inbound_import_empty`. When the run cannot be written at all (the account lost `run`: `inbound_run_refused`; the project was archived meanwhile: `inbound_project_archived`), the `run.failed` event comes WITHOUT a run, and `GET /runs/{run_id}` stays 404. If the import cannot be queued the call answers 500 `import_enqueue_failed` and the announced run is already failed (`inbound_import_failed`): a replay of the call names it. A known `external_id` answers 200 with the existing case and its run (the pending one while its import runs); with `?rerun=1` the picks are added to that case and a new run starts after their import. 409 `import_running` while another import holds the case (a multipart `?rerun=1` too).

get.summary: The views of a run
get.description: Every view the run’s workflow declares, plus any view the run holds rows for. `built` is false for a declared view the run has not produced (yet). `backing` says how the rows are stored; the view routes answer the same way for both.

view.description: The name the view routes take.

post.summary: Filter and sort a run view to an ordered list of row seqs
post.description: `filter` selects rows (`search` text, `facets` values per field, `ranges` min/max per field); `sort` orders them (`field`, `dir`). Returns the matching `seqs` in order and, with `join`, the ids of the findings joined to them. Fetch the rows themselves with the window route, at most 500 seqs per call. List a run’s views (and whether each is built) with GET /runs/{id}/views.

get.summary: Page through the rows of a run view
get.description: Returns a bare JSON array of rows ordered by `seq`. To read a whole view, start with `seq_from=0` and repeat with `seq_from` set to the last returned `seq` plus one until an array shorter than `limit` (or empty) comes back. Rows carry no findings here; use the window route for those. List a run’s views (and whether each is built) with GET /runs/{id}/views.

post.summary: Record a reviewer’s verdict on one row of a run view
post.description: A row approval is a person’s sign-off on one row of a run’s view (a document–booking link, an orphan document or an orphan booking). Send the chosen `option` (or `verdict`, the same field under its first name): one of the options the view’s review declaration offers, or for a view that declares none `cleared`, `flagged` (needs a `note`) or `needs_review`. Values of the declared review fields go in `input`, by field key. Name the run (`runId`) and the view (`view`), then the row by the `rowKey` the view rows hand out, and send the row’s current `token`. If the row has changed since the token was issued the call is refused with 409 `stale_snapshot`, whose body carries the fresh `token` and `snapshot`. An option the row does not offer is refused (400 `row_parked`, or `option_not_offered` with its `reason`); a field value that does not fit its type is 400 `invalid_field` naming the `field`; a requirement of the option that does not hold is 400 with its code (`note_required_for_flag`, `findings_not_judged`, else `requirement_failed`) and `failures` (`message`, `field`). An option whose effect rejects the row’s open findings needs `confirmEffects` (or `rejectOpenFindings`) true: without it the default `cleared` is refused with 400 `findings_not_judged`, a declared option with 409 `effect_needs_confirmation` (`effect`, `findings`: how many). A person’s new review replaces their own earlier one; reviews by different people stand side by side. An option key the view does not declare is 400 `unknown_option` when sent as `option`; sent only as `verdict` it is 400 `invalid_input`, as it always was. With `portedFrom` the option, note and fields of an approval in another case of the same project are adopted instead; an option the view no longer declares, or does not offer on this row, is 400 `option_not_offered`, and an `option`/`verdict` naming another option than the adopted one is 400 `invalid_input`. The caller needs the `review` permission on the case’s project.

get.summary: A webhook's newest deliveries
How far a run has come
get.description: The run's live progress as the worker last stored it (at most every 5 s, and once more when nothing runs any more), for a bridge to show a run that is still `sent` or `running`. There is no total and no percentage: cached, skipped and per-document nodes make a count from the graph misleading. `running` lists the nodes in flight; `items_done` / `item_count` are exact for a node that runs per item, null otherwise. A queued run (and a run with no stored progress) answers `updated_at: null`, `running: []` and null counts; a finished run its final status, the last snapshot's counts and `running: []`. The worker refreshes the snapshot at least every 10 s for as long as the run is `running`, so `stale` (the run is `running` and its snapshot, or with none its start, is older than 30 s) means no progress was written for 30 s: usually the worker is gone, sometimes only its live-progress connection (the run may still finish). Counts are the current attempt's: a resumed run counts from its resume. Any token that may read the run; not for a `sync`-scoped token.

updated_at.description: When the worker last stored progress; null when it never did.

items_done.description: Items of this node finished so far.

nodes_finished.description: Distinct nodes that reached an end (succeeded, failed, skipped, waiting for review).
